games.title: Kingdom Sorter
games.skillName: Classifying living things into broad groups
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to describe how living things are classified into broad groups according to common observable characteristics and based on similarities and differences, including micro-organisms, plants and animals
games.instruction: Tap the group each living thing belongs to.
games.hint: Not quite. Does it have a backbone, does it make flowers, or is it too tiny to see? Try again.

questions.ask: A bacterium
A toadstool
A fern
A daisy
A snail
A salmon
A clump of moss
An earthworm

games.title: Adaptation Spotter
games.skillName: Spotting how living things are adapted to their habitat
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify how animals and plants are adapted to suit their environment in different ways and that adaptation may lead to evolution
games.instruction: Tap the one that does not belong.
games.hint: Think about where this living thing lives and what would really help it survive there.

questions.ask: Which is NOT an adaptation that helps a camel live in the desert?
Which is NOT an adaptation that helps a polar bear survive in the Arctic?
Which is NOT an adaptation that helps a cactus survive in a dry desert?
Which is NOT an adaptation that helps a fish live in water?
Which is NOT an adaptation that helps an owl hunt at night?
Which is NOT an adaptation that helps a woodpecker feed on insects inside trees?
Which of these is NOT a characteristic inherited from your parents?
Which is NOT an adaptation that helps a duck live on a pond?

games.title: Light Line Check
games.skillName: Explaining how we see objects and why shadows form
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise that light appears to travel in straight lines; use the idea that light travels in straight lines to explain that objects are seen because they give out or reflect light into the eye; explain that we see things because light travels from light sources to our eyes or from light sources to objects and then to our eyes; use the idea that light travels in straight lines to explain why shadows have the same shape as the objects that cast them
games.instruction: Tap True or False for each statement about light.
games.hint: Remember that light travels in straight lines, and we only see things when light enters our eyes.

questions.ask: Light travels in straight lines.
We see objects because light travels out of our eyes and onto them.
We can see a book because light from a source reflects off it into our eyes.
A shadow has the same shape as the object that casts it.
A mirror is a light source because it makes its own light.
In a room with no light at all, you could still see a red ball.
The Moon is a light source.
A periscope uses mirrors to reflect light into your eye.

games.title: Heart and Blood
games.skillName: Naming parts of the circulatory system and their jobs
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify and name the main parts of the human circulatory system, and describe the functions of the heart, blood vessels and blood; describe the ways in which nutrients and water are transported within animals, including humans
games.instruction: Tap the word that fills the gap.
games.hint: Think about the job each part of the circulatory system does, then try again.

questions.ask: The ___ pumps blood all around the body.
Blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart are called ___.
Blood vessels that carry blood back to the heart are called ___.
Tiny blood vessels with very thin walls are called ___.
Blood picks up oxygen as it passes through the ___.
Nutrients from digested food pass into the blood through the walls of the small ___.
Blood carries water, nutrients and ___ to every cell in the body.
The heart is a strong organ made mostly of ___.

games.title: Changes Over Time
games.skillName: Ordering how fossils form and how species change
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise that living things have changed over time and that fossils provide information about living things that inhabited the Earth millions of years ago
games.instruction: Tap what comes next in the sequence.
games.hint: Think about the order things happen over thousands or millions of years, then try again.

questions.ask: Animal dies → Body sinks to the seabed → Soft parts rot away → ?
Bones covered by sediment → More layers build up on top → ?
Bones buried in rock → Minerals replace the bones → Rock above is worn away → ?
Leaf falls into mud → Mud covers the leaf → Mud slowly hardens → ?
Dinosaur walks in soft mud → Footprint dries hard → Sand fills the print → ?
Giraffes with longer necks reach more food → They survive and breed → Young inherit long necks → ?
Soot darkens tree bark → Birds spot pale moths easily → More dark moths survive → ?
Island seeds get harder → Finches with strong beaks eat more → They have more chicks → ?

games.title: Symbol Sleuth
games.skillName: Recognising the symbols used in circuit diagrams
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to use recognised symbols when representing a simple circuit in a diagram
games.instruction: Read the clues and tap the circuit part they describe.
games.hint: Picture each circuit symbol in your head and match it to the clues.

questions.ask: My symbol is a circle with a cross inside. I light up when current flows. What am I?
My symbol is a long thin line beside a short thick line. I push the current. What am I?
My symbol shows a hinged line lifted away from a gap. The circuit is broken. What am I?
My symbol shows a hinged line touching across the gap. The circuit is complete. What am I?
My symbol is a circle with the letter M inside. I make things spin. What am I?
My symbol is a plain straight line. I join components so current can flow. What am I?
My symbol is two or more cells joined together. I give a bigger voltage. What am I?
My symbol looks like a dome with two legs. I make a noise when current flows. What am I?

games.title: Circuit Predictor
games.skillName: Predicting how cells and switches change components
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to associate the brightness of a lamp or the volume of a buzzer with the number and voltage of cells used in the circuit; compare and give reasons for variations in how components function, including the brightness of bulbs, the loudness of buzzers and the on/off position of switches
games.instruction: Tap what you think will happen to the circuit.
games.hint: Think about how the voltage, the number of cells and the switch change the current, then try again.

questions.ask: What will happen if you add a second cell to a circuit with one cell and one bulb?
What will happen if you add a second bulb in the same loop as the first, with one cell?
What will happen if you open the switch in a working circuit with a buzzer?
What happens when you swap a 1.5 V cell for a 3 V battery in a buzzer circuit?
What happens when you use two cells instead of three in a bulb circuit?
What will happen if you turn the cell round in a circuit with one bulb?
What will happen if one wire comes loose from the cell in a bulb circuit?
What happens when you close the switch in a circuit with a cell and a motor?

games.title: Evolution Words
games.skillName: Using the vocabulary of evolution and inheritance
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise that living things produce offspring of the same kind, but normally offspring vary and are not identical to their parents; identify how animals and plants are adapted to suit their environment in different ways and that adaptation may lead to evolution
games.instruction: Tap the science word that matches the meaning.
games.hint: Read the meaning carefully and think about which science word describes it best.

questions.ask: The young produced by a living thing
Differences between living things of the same kind
Characteristics being passed on from parents to their offspring
A feature that helps a living thing survive in its environment
The slow change in living things over many, many generations
The preserved remains or traces of a living thing from long ago, found in rock
When every member of a species has died out
The process where the best-suited living things survive and breed

games.title: Healthy Choices
games.skillName: Comparing how diet, exercise and drugs affect the body
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise the impact of diet, exercise, drugs and lifestyle on the way their bodies function
games.instruction: Tap the best answer to each question.
games.hint: Think about what each choice does to your heart, lungs and body, then try again.

questions.ask: Which activity makes your heart beat the fastest?
Which drink is the healthiest choice for quenching thirst every day?
Which of these contains the most sugar?
Which is the most harmful to the heart and lungs?
Which food is the best source of protein for growth and repair?
Which habit would best help a child's body rest, recover and grow?
Whose heart is likely to beat the slowest when resting?
Which drink is most likely to damage the liver if drunk often?

games.title: Shadow Lab
games.skillName: Planning a fair test and measuring shadows accurately
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to plan different types of scientific enquiries, including recognising and controlling variables; take measurements with increasing accuracy and precision, taking repeat readings; record results using tables and line graphs; and report conclusions
games.instruction: Tap the best way to investigate shadows like a scientist.
games.hint: Think about fair tests, the right equipment and changing only one thing at a time.

questions.ask: Which would you use to measure the length of a shadow?
You test how the torch's distance affects shadow size. What do you change?
In that test, what should you keep the same to make it fair?
Which is the best way to record shadow lengths at different torch distances?
Which graph best shows how shadow length changes as the torch moves away?
Why should you measure each shadow three times?
After testing you write: the closer the torch, the bigger the shadow. What is this?
Shadow readings were 10 cm, 11 cm, 12 cm and 30 cm. Which looks like an error?
